affected_system: multimodal evacuation, assisted transport, and emergency access network
alternatives: rank verified high-consequence candidates for emergency mobility readiness investment portfolio
select a risk-, equity-, and lifecycle-balanced portfolio for emergency mobility readiness investment portfolio
pair multi-hazard clearance and equity portfolio optimization with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Evacuation demand, assistance eligibility, vehicle capacity, route state, and hazard timing are versioned.
Compliance, household departure, and network degradation remain observed inputs or bounded scenarios.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: fund only already-committed work for emergency mobility readiness investment portfolio.

constraints.description: The evacuation and emergency mobility prioritize must respect declared capital, operating, maintenance, and delivery budgets.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: emergency transportation coordinator and incident commander
decision_question: Which route, fleet, communication, power, and accessibility upgrades most improve safe clearance?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The evacuation and emergency mobility prioritize must respect declared capital, operating, maintenance, and delivery budgets.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for emergency mobility readiness investment portfolio passes documented checks for cost, benefit, service life, dependencies, deliverability, and maintenance burden.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: multi-hazard clearance and equity portfolio optimization
independence_key.primary_outcome: expected people beyond safe clearance capacity

intended_claim: A versioned prioritize design for comparing declared alternatives affecting emergency mobility readiness investment portfolio, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: expected people beyond safe clearance capacity
distributional gap in expected people beyond safe clearance capacity
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not call modeled clearance improvements saved lives or completed readiness work.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for emergency mobility readiness investment portfolio passes documented checks for cost, benefit, service life, dependencies, deliverability, and maintenance burden.

title: Prioritize emergency mobility readiness investments
transportability_risks: Hazards, vehicle ownership, disability access, road topology, trust, and compliance differ.
Registration systems may undercount people needing assistance.
